note: mapping_basis=reconstructed: no source file labels the columns. data/CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020.R does select(starts_with('DSES')) + pivot_longer, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (ex.dataset.csv / pa.dataset.csv headers DSES_1, DSES_10..DSES_15) -- no positional step -- but the columns carry only a number, and that number is on the CZECH 15-item DSES (Malinakova et al. 2018, Ceskoslovenska psychologie 62 Suppl.1), which is Underwood's 16 items minus item 5 ('I find comfort in my religion or spirituality', dropped for r=.92 with item 4). Under that renumbering CZ1..CZ15 = Underwood 1-4,6-16, so the 7 administered items are Underwood 1, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. Only 7 of the 15 items were administered in this study. TEXT: no wording is published in the deposit or in the source paper (Sandora et al. 2021 IJERPH 18:10337 never mentions the DSES), so the words are Underwood's canonical English, transcribed verbatim from Table 1 of Underwood 2011, Religions 2(1):29-50 (CC BY 3.0) -- including its missing terminal period on item 15 and its anchor labels 'Not close'/'Somewhat close'/'Very close'/'As close as possible'. RIGHTS: the wording was copied from a CC BY 3.0 article, which under the ECR-R ruling (itemtext_standard.md) is the licence that governs, so it ships; but Underwood states instrument-level restrictions -- 'Registration is required to use the scale, which is free for non-profit use' (dsescale.org) and 'Permission of author required to distribute or copy' (Fetzer self-measures compendium copy) -- so every row carries wording_rights=NC. FLAG FOR BEN: that second sentence is a redistribution bar of the same shape as the WHOQOL clause; itemtext_standard.md says the WHOQOL ruling must not be extended to another instrument without asking, so this table ships under the default rule and should be withdrawn if the stricter reading is adopted.
